problem.name: Isomorphism to the standard integer lattice
problem.statement_latex: Given the Gram matrix of a lattice $L$ promised isometric to $\mathbb Z^n$, recover an orthonormal integral lattice basis, equivalently an explicit isometry $L\to\mathbb Z^n$. This is the standard-integer-lattice case of lattice isomorphism, relevant to signature constructions such as HAWK. Complexity is measured in quantum gate time with the stated QRAM access and in classical bit-operation time, suppressing polynomial input-precision factors.
problem.statement_text: Given the Gram matrix of a lattice $L$ promised isometric to $\mathbb Z^n$, recover an orthonormal integral lattice basis, equivalently an explicit isometry $L\to\mathbb Z^n$. Complexity is measured in quantum gate time with the stated QRAM access and in classical bit-operation time, suppressing polynomial input-precision factors.

quantum.headline_latex: $2^{0.1235n+o(n)}$ time, Ducas reduction with the Hhan--Kim--Kim--Laarhoven SVP subroutine.
quantum.headline_text: $2^{0.1235n+o(n)}$ time, Ducas reduction with the Hhan–Kim–Kim–Laarhoven SVP subroutine.
quantum.details_latex: The exponent is obtained by substituting the $2^{0.247d+o(d)}$ quantum SVP bound into the reduction to dimension $d\simeq n/2$. It is a direct consequence of the two results. The Aggarwal--Chen--Kumar--Shen implementation gives a separately quantified tradeoff: $2^{0.417n+o(n)}$ time, $2^{0.147n+o(n)}$ QRAM, $2^{0.25n+o(n)}$ classical storage and polynomial additional qubits. Both computations recover norm-one directions sufficient to reconstruct the integral isometry.

classical.headline_latex: $2^{0.2045n+o(n)}$ time, the same reduction with classical superlattice SVP.
classical.headline_text: $2^{0.2045n+o(n)}$ time, the same reduction with classical superlattice SVP.
classical.details_latex: Substitution of the $2^{0.409d+o(d)}$ classical SVP theorem gives the displayed exponent. Classical discrete-Gaussian SVP with $2^{d+o(d)}$ time yields the alternative $2^{n/2+o(n)}$ bound. The reduction and output task are identical in both comparisons; the dimension-halving exponents retain the assumptions and storage costs of their chosen SVP subroutines.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant in the lattice rank. The quantitative comparison follows from the matched classical and quantum shortest-vector algorithms.

evidence.description_latex: Partial evidence for separation. The two fastest displayed exponents depend on the 2026 superlattice preprint; the $0.417$ quantum implementation has a published rigorous resource analysis.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant computation with exponential storage is required for these algorithms. The published construction distinguishes polynomial logical workspace, $2^{0.147n+o(n)}$ QRAM cells and $2^{0.25n+o(n)}$ classical memory; the superlattice substitution inherits its own exponential time-space requirement.
